source_type: UK Parliament first-party official JSON endpoint observed through web text rendering; original bytes not downloaded or SHA256 authenticated
bias: Top 12 CLOSED petitions by signature totals, not random or representative. Individual people may sign multiple petitions.
A: Does at least one of twelve closed petitions with 100k signatures fail to have scheduled/completed debate, or are all twelve recorded for debate?

B.H1: At least one without debate despite 100k

C.execution: Inspect 12 official API threshold crossing and scheduled_debate_date and debate_outcome_at, compute interval from exact crossing to UTC midnight of scheduled_debate_date; compare median and 90d benchmark. Do not equate scheduled date to actual completed until Hansard crosscheck in C05.

F: H1 not found in selected 12. Cannot assert that every petition reaching 100k is debated; the rule only promises consideration. Delays > 90 days in half the selected cases; no required deadline inferred. All 12 have API outcome timestamps, but separate Hansard independently opened only first 5.
G: Petitions top signed; survivorship/outcome selection, publication-censoring. One debate can involve multiple petitions, don't count one per unique parliamentary sitting without checking.
J: Validate subset of actual Hansard debate pages independently.
